summary: Red team of the accepted library audit AUDIT-09. It covers five roadmaps (ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity, EffectiveDiophantineMethods, FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems, HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions, InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups), with 34 layers, 136 targets (105 absent, 30 partial, 1 mathlib), 290 cited declarations and the duplicates lists. 23 findings: none high, 8 medium, 15 low. No target's status changes and every layer verdict holds. All 290 citations exist at the cited file and line. The medium findings: CM.5's note says Tau Ceti has the endomorphism ring of a Weierstrass curve, but Isogeny.Hom W W is only a monoid with zero plus an additive group with right distributivity, not a ring. IG.6 misses Tau Ceti's proof that inertia generates the Galois group of a number field, the input Mathlib's Morse-polynomial TODO asks for. IG.5 misstates the nearest notion to regularity, since IsIntegrallyClosedIn with Tau Ceti's constant-field theory is available. Five duplicate omissions: PolynomialGaloisGroups Layer 6 (certified C_n and D_n labels over ℚ) for IG.4 and IG.6; the new MordellLawrenceVenkatesh roadmap's LV.8 (Hurwitz spaces, Kodaira–Parshin) for IG.5 and RP.4; LV.11 (Faltings's theorem) for RP.4; LV.3 (Strassmann) for ED.4; LV.1 (Faltings's finiteness lemma) for R28.5. The low findings are further uncited declarations (comp_eq_zero_iff, Scheme.Hom.image, K(S,n) finiteness, structure constants, the profinite fibre-functor equivalence), two fit labels, the misdescribed hypotheses of fg_point, a false parenthetical, one wrong duplicate (R11.6) and further missed duplicates.
checked: Every cited declaration: all 290 citations (245 distinct declarations) were resolved against a fresh declaration index of the pinned trees (Mathlib 082e2d3: 246,008 declarations; Tau Ceti f790474: 70,802), built with research/blueprint/index_declarations.py. All exist at the cited file within three lines of the cited line. The two the index misses because of namespace reconstruction, fermatLastTheoremFour (Mathlib/NumberTheory/FLT/Four.lean:267) and TauCeti.FiniteLocallyFreeCommAffineGroupSchemeCat.cartierDuality (CartierDuality/FiniteLocallyFree.lean:232), were opened by hand. Three checkers then opened every declaration at its line with the section's variable lines and docstrings and compared it with its target, note and fit label; for the CM, R28, ED and RP layers the cited Tau Ceti files were also checked for sorry (only docstring hits).

Every layer: all 34 stage descriptions were read in data/atlas.json (the per-roadmap extracts in research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/ match). Each target list was compared with its stage's constructions and acceptance items (no omitted target whose library status matters was found), and each verdict with its targets: IG.0 is partly built, 3 layers are process and the rest are not built, all consistent. Both roadmap summaries and all 61 review corrections were re-read, and the corrected citations were re-verified at the pins.

Every absent target was searched by concept and synonym in the index (grep -i -P) and in both source trees (grep -rn -i). The searches covered the terms of each target: for CM, orders/conductor/Pic, CM types/reflex, the j-function and class polynomials, the uniformisation, Hecke characters, the Tate module, supersingularity, class fields and Chebotarev; for R28, polarisations, Néron models, p-divisible groups, Faltings height, Zarhin, Shafarevich, Jordan–Zassenhaus and Poincaré reducibility; for ED, Sturm/isolating intervals, LLL/HNF/PSLQ, Baker/Matveev, the p-adic logarithm, S-units/Thue, Sha/torsors, Chabauty/Coleman/Strassmann and reduction maps; for RP, Northcott/Weil/local heights, Pic, the Hilbert symbol/Hasse–Minkowski, Brauer groups and adelic points, Riemann–Hurwitz, Parshin, Faltings, Mordell–Lang and Bogomolov; for IG, Galois categories and fibre functors, finite étale, Ẑ, tame and wild ramification, Hilbert irreducibility, Dedekind's cycle types, Riemann existence/Belyi/dessins, Hurwitz/braid actions, rigidity and structure constants, embedding problems, Shafarevich and Scholz–Reichardt, regular extensions, Artin–Schreier and Selmer polynomials. Only the findings above change a note; every other absent target is confirmed absent.

Every duplicates entry (39 for CM and R28, 36 for ED and RP, 29 for IG) was checked: each named layer exists in data/atlas.json and its description was read; all but R11.6 plan the stated targets. Missed duplicates were searched by keyword over all 1968 atlas stage descriptions and the six new roadmaps in research/blueprint/roadmaps/*.json. The candidates rejected as consumers or out of scope are listed in the report.

The reviewed decomposition data/decompositions/FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems.json (32 nodes, all implementationStatus unchecked): the only library name any node gives, NumberField.finite_of_discr_bdd, agrees with the audit.
data/library-coverage.json (the merged reviewed coverage) was read only for comparison; the findings are stated against the audit file, which the fixer edits.

findings.where: research/blueprint/audit/AUDIT-09.result.json — ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity:CM.5, target 'Endomorphism-ring verification as a separate certificate'
findings.claim: The note says 'The endomorphism ring of a Weierstrass curve exists in Tau Ceti'. It does not: Tau Ceti's Isogeny.Hom W W is a monoid with zero under composition and, separately, an additive group. Only right distributivity (g + g')∘f = g∘f + g'∘f is proved; there is no comp_add, no Ring or Semiring instance, and the source says the ring structure is not built. The only declaration cited, instNontrivialEnd, says End has two distinct elements. So a design reading the note would treat End(E) as an available ring, whereas the ring structure (left distributivity via the point map toPointHom) is itself work to plan.
findings.evidence: Tau Ceti f790474, TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Isogeny/Hom/Basic.lean:30–31: 'Addition is not defined here, so `Hom W W` is a monoid with zero rather than a ring.'; :322–325: 'The endomorphisms of `W` form a monoid with zero under composition … The additive structure that would make it a ring is not built here. -/ noncomputable instance : MonoidWithZero (Hom W₁ W₁)'; TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Isogeny/Hom/Add.lean:204 'noncomputable instance : AddCommGroup (Hom W₁ W₂)' and :282 'theorem add_comp … : (g + g').comp f = g.comp f + g'.comp f'. grep over TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Isogeny/ finds no comp_add and no Ring/Semiring instance on Hom. The point map needed for left distributivity is named only as a future target (Isogeny/IntermediateRing/Basic.lean:76–80). The cited instNontrivialEnd (TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Isogeny/Hom/Basic.lean:350) has docstring 'The carrier has more than one element'.
findings.fix: Replace the note by: 'Tau Ceti's `Isogeny.Hom W W` is a monoid with zero under composition (no zero divisors) and an additive group, with only `(g+g')∘f = g∘f + g'∘f` proved; left distributivity, hence a ring End(E), is not proved (the point map `toPointHom` is not built). End(E) is neither a ring nor identified with an order, and no algorithm or certificate computes it.' Add {name: TauCeti.Isogeny.Hom.add_comp, library: tauceti, file: TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Isogeny/Hom/Add.lean, line: 282, fit: related}. Status stays absent.

findings.where: research/blueprint/audit/AUDIT-09.result.json — InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.5, target 'Hurwitz moduli spaces with braid/Nielsen-class components, descent and…'
findings.claim: The note says 'regularity of a field extension is not defined; the nearest notion is Mathlib's scheme-theoretic geometric integrality of a morphism'. That misstates the nearest notion. The field-level content of regularity is in the libraries. 'k algebraically closed in F' is Mathlib's IsIntegrallyClosedIn k F, and Tau Ceti proves its equivalence with algebraicClosure k F = ⊥ and the linear disjointness of F from finite separable constant extensions. In characteristic 0, the setting over ℚ(t) of IG.2 and IG.5, that is exactly regularity. The atlas already uses this predicate as the regular-extension hypothesis for Belyi pairs.
findings.evidence: TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/ConstantField.lean:95 'theorem algebraicClosure_eq_bot_iff_isIntegrallyClosedIn : algebraicClosure k F = ⊥ ↔ IsIntegrallyClosedIn k F' (variables line 56: {k F} [Field k] [Field F] [Algebra k F]); TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/GeometricDegree.lean:251 'theorem finrank_constantCompositum_eq_finrank_of_isSeparable (hex : IsIntegrallyClosedIn k F) [FiniteDimensional k k'] [Algebra.IsSeparable k k'] : Module.finrank F (constantCompositum F k' F') = Module.finrank k k''. Stage tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/BelyiMaps#layer-9-algebraic-belyi-pairs-and-algebraization: 'an algebraic Belyi pair is a function field F/k … with exact constants IsIntegrallyClosedIn k F'.
findings.fix: Add {TauCeti.algebraicClosure_eq_bot_iff_isIntegrallyClosedIn, tauceti, TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/ConstantField.lean, 95, related} and {TauCeti.finrank_constantCompositum_eq_finrank_of_isSeparable, tauceti, TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/GeometricDegree.lean, 251, related}. Replace the clause by: 'regularity is not a named predicate, but its field-level content is available: k algebraically closed in F is Mathlib's IsIntegrallyClosedIn k F, which Tau Ceti identifies with algebraicClosure k F = ⊥ and shows forces linear disjointness from finite separable constant extensions (in characteristic 0, regularity); scheme-theoretically Mathlib has geometric integrality of a morphism.' Status unchanged.

findings.where: research/blueprint/audit/AUDIT-09.result.json — InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.3, target 'The rational rigidity criterion: rigid, rational conjugacy-class triples…'
findings.claim: The note lists 'the count of triples with product one' as absent. Tau Ceti's structureConstant is that count up to a class size: #{(x,y,z) ∈ Cᵢ×Cⱼ×Cₖ : xyz = 1} = |Cₖ| · structureConstant Cᵢ Cⱼ Cₖ⁻¹. What is absent is its expression through characters (Frobenius's formula), the count of generating triples, rigidity, and rationality of classes.
findings.evidence: TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/CharacterTable/ClassSum/StructureConstants.lean:62–64 '/-- The number of factorizations `x * y = g`, for `x ∈ Cᵢ`, `y ∈ Cⱼ`, and any representative `g` of `Cₖ`. This is independent of the representative by simultaneous conjugation. -/ def structureConstant (Cᵢ Cⱼ Cₖ : ConjClasses G) : ℕ'.
findings.fix: Add {TauCeti.structureConstant, tauceti, TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/CharacterTable/ClassSum/StructureConstants.lean, 64, related}. Note: 'Tau Ceti has class-sum structure constants (structureConstant Cᵢ Cⱼ Cₖ counts xy = g with x ∈ Cᵢ, y ∈ Cⱼ for fixed g ∈ Cₖ, so product-one triples in given classes are a class size times a structure constant) and the Galois action on character values; the character formula for that count, the count of generating triples, rigidity, rationality of classes and the criterion are absent.'
